business.title: Measurement of contextual factors in clinical practice and research: development of an expert-informed toolkit
business.description: Contextual factors (CFs) can influence therapeutic encounters and clinical outcomes, yet their measurement remains fragmented, lacking a unified framework to guide tool selection. To identify, appraise, and synthesize CF measurement instruments into an expert-informed clinical toolkit and identify current measurement gaps. An international panel of 15 experts evaluated 227 instruments across five domains (patient/practitioner characteristics, relational dynamics, environment, and treatment) using a hybrid COSMIN-informed appraisal design. Instruments were screened for content validity and psychometric robustness. Twenty instruments were selected for inclusion in the toolkit. Despite identifying high-quality instruments for stable traits, our analysis revealed critical measurement gaps in dynamic, state-responsive processes. Specifically, there is an absence of validated, clinically feasible tools for capturing real-time clinician affective states, non-verbal synchrony, therapeutic touch, and moment-to-moment environmental or procedural interactions. This study provides the first expert-informed framework for assessing CFs. Future research should prioritize developing state-responsive instruments capable of capturing these dynamic elements as they unfold in real-world settings to better understand the contextual drivers of recovery.

science.title: Shear strength behavior of frozen unsaturated sands under thermal loads
science.description: Understanding the mechanical behavior of frozen unsaturated sand under thermal gradients is crucial for the design and maintenance of infrastructure in permafrost regions. In this study the shear strength of Ottawa sand under varying temperatures, degrees of saturation, and loading conditions is investigated. A series of laboratory experiments were performed to measure the shear strength of Ottawa sand using direct simple shear equipment placed in a temperature controlled environmental chamber. During the experiments, soil temperatures and stress–strain curves were recorded, and they were analyzed to determine the strength behavior. Results show that shear strength increases with decreasing temperature, increasing ice content, strain rate, and normal stress. A significant increase in strength was observed with increasing initial degree of saturation, attributed to higher ice content acting as a cementing agent within the soil matrix. A modified Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion was developed by integrating soil freezing curves to account for the effects of ice content on both cohesion and friction angle. The model exhibited strong predictive capability (R2 = 0.98) for shear strength under thermal loads. These findings provide a robust framework for assessing the stability of geotechnical structures in cold regions and highlight the critical role of ice content in frozen soil behavior.

science.title: Stem Cell Reports named official meeting Journal of ASSCR 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting
science.description:
Stem Cell Reports, the official journal of the International Society for Stem Cell Research (ISSCR), has been named the Official Meeting Journal of the Australasian Society for Stem Cell Research (ASSCR) 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting, taking place 9-11 November 2026 at The Glasshouse in Melbourne, Australia.
Under the theme “Brewing Innovation,” ASSCR 2026 will bring together researchers and leaders in stem cell science and regenerative medicine to share new discoveries, explore emerging technologies, and foster scientific collaboration across the Australasian research community and beyond.
